clauses: With %.3f it would print 3.142 and no spaces

paths.label: shown
paths.logic: Changing the precision changes only the printed digits, not the stored value. Changing the width changes only the padding. A width smaller than the converted text is ignored, so nothing is truncated.

paths.label: shown
paths.logic: One call appends one formatted string to standard output and adds no newline unless \n or %n is in the format. The stored values of the arguments do not change (only their printed form is rounded).

paths.label: shown
paths.quote: With %.3f it would print 3.142 and no spaces
paths.logic: The output is the formatted text. printf("%7.5f", Math.PI) gives 3.14159, printf("PI is approximately %.2f\n", Math.PI) gives `PI is approximately 3.14` and a newline, and printf("%5d", 42) gives `   42`. Rounding is half-up.
